title: Magnetic circular dichroism of THz modes and selection rules of Raman-active optical phonons in the polar altermagnet candidate \ce{Mn2Mo3O8}
authors: F. Schilberth, K. Vasin, M. Knauft, M. Kondákor, M. Vuckovic, N. Herrmann, K. Penc, M. Minola, B. Keimer, V. A. Martinez, K. Panda, A. A. Sirenko, L. Prodan, V. Tsurkan, A. A. Tsirlin, I. Kézsmárki, J. Deisenhofer
abstract: We investigated the magnetic and vibrational excitations in the collinear altermagnet candidate \ce{Mn2Mo3O8} by temperature dependent Raman scattering and magneto-optical THz time-domain transmission spectroscopy. By comparison to \textit{ab initio} calculations accurately capturing the eigenfrequencies of the vibrational eigenmodes, we identify all optical phonons, including the lowest-lying Raman modes of $A_1$ and $E_2$ type, which had remained elusive in a previous Raman study. Moreover, we compare the selection rules for optically active phonons in the paramagnetic and the magnetically ordered phases of \ce{Mn2Mo3O8} and analyze the Raman selection rules with respect to pseudo-angular momentum conservation. No evidence of the expected splitting of the degenerate paramagnetic $E_2$ optical phonons into modes with circular polarization upon magnetic ordering could be resolved, likely due to weak spin-orbit coupling typical for Mn$^{2+}$. In contrast, we observe strong magnetic circular dichroism at a broad THz excitation band, emerging in the magnetically ordered state. This band, potentially originating from two-magnon excitations, is only electric-dipole active and features a field-dependent two-component fine structure. Its magnetic circular dichroism vanishes above the spin-flop transition at 4~T.
summary: This study characterizes the coupled magnetic and vibrational excitations in Mn2Mo3O8 using THz spectroscopy and Raman scattering. By analyzing selection rules against crystal and magnetic symmetries, the authors identified key optical phonons and observed a characteristic magnetic circular dichroism signal linked to two-magnon excitations that vanishes upon field changes.
main_problem: The study investigates the magnetic and vibrational excitations, specifically THz modes and Raman-active optical phonons, in the polar altermagnet candidate Mn2Mo3O8.
main_result: Strong magnetic circular dichroism was observed at a broad THz excitation band only in the magnetically ordered state, which vanishes above the spin-flop transition. Furthermore, all optical phonons were identified using combined spectroscopic and theoretical analysis.
method: The research combines temperature-dependent Raman scattering and magneto-optical THz time-domain spectroscopy with *ab initio* DFT+U calculations to analyze symmetry constraints.
model_or_system: The physical system is the collinear altermagnet candidate Mn2Mo3O8, whose magnetic and vibrational properties are analyzed across paramagnetic and magnetically ordered phases using group theory applied to corepresentations.
key_observables: Magnetic circular dichroism (MCD) in the THz range, Raman-active optical phonon frequencies ($	ext{A}_1$, $	ext{E}_2$ modes), and selection rules based on pseudo-angular momentum conservation.
important_parameters: The spin-flop transition field (4 T); temperature dependence across magnetic ordering transitions ($T_N = 40 	ext{ K}$); DFT parameters ($	ext{U}_d = 5 	ext{ eV}$, $	ext{J}_d = 1 	ext{ eV}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on comparing experimental results to predictions derived from magnetic point group symmetry and the conservation of pseudo-angular momentum.
figures_summary: Figure 2 shows magnetization vs. T/H, indicating a spin-flop transition around 4 T; Figure 6 displays temperature-dependent absorption spectra related to optical band gaps.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the material's symmetry using corepresentations, first identifying all optical phonons via Raman scattering and comparing selection rules with pseudo-angular momentum conservation. It then uses THz spectroscopy to probe magnetic excitations, observing MCD linked to the magnetic ordering state.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges lattice dynamics (phonons) and magnetism (magnons/MCD) in a strongly correlated oxide system, providing detailed spectroscopic evidence of symmetry breaking upon magnetic ordering, which is crucial for understanding emergent quantum phenomena in solids.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Comparison of the different magnetic structures of (a) Co2Mo3O8/Fe2Mo3O8 and (b) Mn2Mo3O8. While for Co2Mo3O8/Fe2Mo3O8 the compensated antiferromagnetic state comprises four magnetic sublattices within the magnetic point group 6′m′m, Mn2Mo3O8 is described by two magnetic sublattices within the magnetic point group 6m′m′, which allows for ferrimagnetism.

FIG. 2. (a) Magnetization of Mn2Mo3O8 as a function of tempera- ture measured upon heating after zero-field cooling (ZFC) and upon cooling in field (FC), both in a field of H = 100 Oe along the c-axis. (b) Magnetization as a function of magnetic field along the c-axis. The inset zooms in on the hysteresis at low fields.

FIG. 3. Comparison of Raman spectra at 85 K (black) and 5 K (blue) in scattering configurations (a) z(xx)¯z allowing for the observation of E2 and A1 modes, (b) z(xy)¯z corresponding to the irreducible E2 representations of the paramagnetic phase. The determined eigen- frequencies of phonon modes expected for each configuration in the paramagnetic phase are indicated by upward triangles at the bottom of the individual panels. Symbols at the top of the panels indicate modes different from expected modes of the paramagnetic phase as described in the text. (c) and (d): Comparison of Raman spectra in crossed circular polarization configurations z(σ+σ−)¯z and z(σ−σ+)¯z at 5 K and 85 K.

FIG. 4. (a) Temperature dependence of the absorption coefficient α in Mn2Mo3O8 for light polarization configuration Eω,Hω ⊥c cross- ing into the magnetically ordered state at TN = 41 K. (b) Comparison of the absorption difference ∆α = α(5 K)−α(60 K) (black) and the lowest-lying E2(1) Raman mode (blue) in the magnetically ordered state at T = 5 K.

FIG. 5. Magnetic field dependence of absorption difference spectra for (a) right circularly polarized light (σ+), (b) left circularly polarized light (σ−) and (c) the difference of right and left circularly polarized spectra σ+ −σ−. Panels (d) and (e) show the zero-field absorption spectra for σ+ and σ−, where (1) corresponds to the first zero-field cooled spectra, (2) to the spectrum taken after the sweep to +7 T, (3) to the one taken after heating to 60 K and zero-field cooling again down to 5 K, and (4) to the one taken after the sweep to -7 T. (f) Magnetic field dependence of the peak frequencies of TM1 and TM2 in comparison to the modulus of the magnetization shown in Fig. 2(b).
